chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Muhammad from Ibn Faddal from Safwan al-Jammal from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding His Exalted and Mighty saying, 'For the petitioner and the deprived,' he said, 'The deprived is the one who has been deprived of the effort of his hand in buying and selling.'
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of 'al-mahroom' (the deprived) in the context of Zakat according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) offers a nuanced exegetical definition of 'al-mahroom' (the deprived) in Quran 9:60, specifying them as those whose hands are 'deprived' of capital for trade and commerce. This interpretation, transmitted via the chain of Safwan al-Jammal, reflects the Shia scholarly tradition of linking Zakat eligibility to economic capacity rather than mere poverty, ensuring aid reaches those structurally excluded from market participation.
